title: Baseball: pitching, White Sox and Oliver in the bleachers
summary: He worked out as a pitcher with the White Sox while hearing Oliver's band at the ballpark, played until 1949, and pitched for Harry James' team.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: You know, I've been wondering, Mr. Curt, did you hear any bands at ball games?

Oh, yeah, sure. I used to work out with the White Sox and Joe Oliver, Joe Oliver used to have the band in the bleachers. And you could hear Joe Oliver all over that ballpark. And there used to be a big negro there, and he had a certain yell. And you could hear him all over the ballpark. I forget. I don't even know who he was. At that time, I could listen to Joe while I was working out with the White Sox. I was a pitcher.
Mm-hmm. I guess you told me once I'd forgotten. Mm-hmm. Did you definitely give up baseball then?
Oh, I gave that. Well, I was playing ball up to 1949 when I threw my arm out. Oh, really? I was playing ball up in 1949. I was working out.
You had a team in Knicks, didn't you? No. I thought the guys around there wouldn't play.
Remember Harry James? They used to have a ball team. Yeah. Some people say it's more of a ball team than a band.

I pitched a game for Harry James' team one time when they were at the Astro Hotel in New York. We played the New York City High School Champions. They only beat us about two to one. Oh, really? Yes, we did. Good game. I pitched about six innings. I had it.
